chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, from Uqba ibn Bashir Al-Asadi, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I am Uqba ibn Bashir Al-Asadi, and I am of noble lineage among my people.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not boast to us about your lineage. Indeed, Allah raises by faith (iman) those whom people consider lowly when they are believers, and lowers by disbelief (kufr) those whom people consider noble when they are disbelievers. So there is no superiority for anyone over anyone except by piety (taqwa).'
ai.seo_question: What is the basis of superiority over others in Islam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Uqba ibn Bashir al-Asadi, known for his prominent lineage, seeks validation from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who redirects the focus from ancestral pride to spiritual merit. The Imam emphasizes that God elevates the humble believer and lowers the proud disbeliever, establishing taqwa (piety) as the sole criterion for superiority, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology's critique of pre-Islamic Arab tribalism. This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the democratization of spiritual status within the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.
